occurrenceRemarks: On 10 June 2025, between 10:00 am and 12:00 pm, at a depth of 28–30 ft at the Koneshvaram Kotuw dive site in Trincomalee, I observed a single moray eel species partially hidden beneath a rock ledge. The eel displayed a distinct row of small silver-white dots along both the upper and lower jaw margins, encircling the mouth area. It remained calm and partially visible, retreating slightly when illuminated. The surrounding habitat included red sponge and coralline algae, with clear visibility and minimal current during the dive.

occurrenceRemarks: The colour of the body is variable, often being light tan, silvery yellow-brown, sandy brown, or honey coloured. The underside of the fish is usually paler, being brown to white in colour. A silver midlateral, longitudinal stripe is normally present. The dorsal fins are dusky on each end, with or without rows of dark brown spots on the second dorsal fin membranes. The caudal fin is dusky terminally, and there is no dark blotch at the base of the pectoral fin as in other sillaginids. All other fins are hyaline, but the anal fin occasionally has a whitish marginand the species having 11 spines in the first dorsal fin, with one spine and 20 to 23 soft rays on the second dorsal fin
